changes.before: If the sent String becomes "finished", what is received before the loop ends?
changes.after: A channel carries values from a sender to a receiver.

before: mpsc::channel creates a multi-producer, single-consumer channel with a Sender and Receiver. send moves this String into the channel; the sending code cannot keep using that moved String. Here only one worker sends, then its sender is dropped when the closure returns.

The for loop receives messages until all senders have been dropped and queued messages drained. Keeping an unused sender alive would keep the loop waiting. After collection, join still explicitly observes the worker’s completion and any panic.
Expected output or behavior: ready. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Explain why cloning a sender and retaining that clone could prevent this receiver loop from terminating. You may trace it without a Rust compiler; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
after: A channel carries values from a sender to a receiver.
The worker sends one String. When it finishes, its sender goes away. The receiving loop stops after it has read the remaining message.
The output is `ready`. The receiver prints the text that the worker sent.
Change the message and follow it from the worker to the loop.

before.question: If the sent String becomes "finished", what is received before the loop ends?
choices: No message, because dropping the sender discards queued values.
ready because channels reuse the original source text
before.explanation: The owned finished String is delivered; dropping the last sender ends iteration only after the queue is drained.

after.question: If the sent String becomes "finished", what is received before the loop ends?
choices: No message, because dropping the sender discards queued values.
ready because channels reuse the original source text
after.explanation: The receiver prints finished, the text actually sent by the worker.
